reasons: Two tests skip when the portfolio output has not been generated, so a green run may not have checked them.

terms.meaning: A generated example output used as fixed test data.
The set of source excerpts that a case's claims are supposed to rest on.
A trusted, hand-chosen example input used for testing.
A shared platform or capability that several processes depend on.
A limit that keeps an adjusted score inside the allowed range.
The combined output across all cases.

used_by: pytest (runs the test file directly; no other callers visible)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and folder paths
sections.what: Loads the generator's constants and effort function, and sets the golden and recorded folder paths.
sections.why: Shared setup for all tests in the file.
sections.watch_out: The generator must be importable from the scripts folder.

sections.name: case
sections.title: Golden case loader
sections.what: Loads a golden case input file by its case id.
sections.why: Tests need the source pack to recompute from.
sections.watch_out: The lookup takes the first match it finds, so duplicate case ids would pick one arbitrarily.

sections.name: recording
sections.title: Recording loader
sections.what: Loads a recorded output file for a given case and schema name.
sections.why: Tests compare recorded outputs with fresh calculations.
sections.watch_out: A missing file raises an error rather than being skipped.

sections.name: case_ids
sections.title: Case id list
sections.what: Lists the ids of every golden case found on disk.
sections.why: Several tests loop over every case.
sections.watch_out: If no cases exist, those tests run over an empty list and report nothing useful.

sections.name: TestTheEffortIsDerivedFromThePack (part 1)
sections.title: Effort derivation checks
sections.what: Checks that recorded effort equals a fresh derivation and its cited excerpts, that the derivation matches hours times volume over productive hours, and that every hour figure appears in the cited excerpts.
sections.why: The docstring says a plausible constant looks like a derivation until it is recalculated.
sections.watch_out: The formula is copied into the test on purpose, so a formula change must be made in both places.

sections.name: TestTheEffortIsDerivedFromThePack: test_a_hypothesised_effort_cites_nothing
sections.title: Unsourced estimates and table coverage
sections.what: Checks that hypothesised estimates cite nothing, and that every case appears in exactly one of the two effort tables.
sections.why: An estimate with no source must be labelled as a hypothesis so the confidence arithmetic charges for it.
sections.watch_out: A case missing from both tables causes an error during generation, and a case in both would silently take whichever branch comes first.

sections.name: TestTheSharedEnablerSplitIsUnequal
sections.title: Shared enabler split is unequal
sections.what: Checks that exactly two cases claim the shared platform enabler, that their effort figures differ, that the larger is more than twice the smaller, and that the portfolio output shows unequal weights.
sections.why: Equal inputs would give a 0.50 to 0.50 split, which would show nothing about whether the weighting reads effort.
sections.watch_out: The last test skips when the portfolio output is missing, so it can be passed over without being run.

sections.name: TestEachCaseAssumesSomethingOfItsOwn
sections.title: Each case has its own assumption
sections.what: Checks that every case has a distinct platform assumption, that the recorded statement matches the case, that a case claiming a prerequisite cites its own pack, that the case with no evidence cannot claim one, and that the prerequisite is not one the estimator already listed.
sections.why: If every case shared one sentence, the mechanism could not be shown doing anything case-specific.
sections.watch_out: The mining case is pinned as unsupported, so changing its data will break this test on purpose.

sections.name: TestTheCalibrationFixtureExercisesTheClamp
sections.title: Calibration fixture exceeds the ceiling
sections.what: Checks that the recorded adjustment pushes the raw score above the top of the scale, and that the portfolio output shows the score clamped to five.
sections.why: A small adjustment would stay inside the scale and never exercise the clamp.
sections.watch_out: The portfolio test skips without the output file and assumes the adjustment it checks is the first one listed.

summary: Checks that the synthesised recordings match the evidence packs they claim to come from, and that the fixture cases differ from each other enough to show the scoring logic working.
purpose: Tests the fixture recordings produced by the synthesis script against the golden case inputs.
why: A figure that looks plausible can pass as a derivation until something recalculates it. The docstring says an earlier flat-value change left the whole suite green while breaking the intended split.
how: Helpers load the golden inputs and the recorded outputs. Tests recompute effort from hours, volume, and productive hours, check that hour figures appear in cited excerpts, check that every case has exactly one basis, check that the shared-enabler split is unequal, check that each case has its own assumption, and check that a calibration adjustment exceeds the top of the scale.
inputs: Golden case input files, recorded output files, and the constants from the synthesis script. Two tests also read the portfolio output if it exists.
outputs: Pass, fail, or skip results from pytest. The file writes no files.
risks: The formula is copied into the test, so changing the generator's formula requires changing this file too. Two tests skip silently when the portfolio output is missing. The case lookup uses the first file it finds.
debug: If effort tests fail, compare the generator's formula with the one in the test. If split or calibration tests skip, run the pipeline to create the portfolio output first.
